title: ISO 15189
shortDescription: The standard NABL actually assesses medical laboratories against — what it requires, why it's structured the way it is, and how it differs from ISO/IEC 17025.
genZNote: Every medical lab's NABL certificate has this exact standard's name printed on it. Know what it actually covers.

sections.heading: What ISO 15189 Is
sections.body: ISO 15189, ‘Medical laboratories — Requirements for quality and competence’, is the international standard NABL (and equivalent accreditation bodies worldwide) use to assess medical laboratories. The current edition is ISO 15189:2022, which replaced the ISO 15189:2012 edition — exams should treat 2022 as current and 2012 as the historical/previous edition. The 2022 edition also folded in point-of-care testing (POCT) requirements that previously sat in a separate standard, and restructured itself to align with ISO/IEC 17025:2017's format.
bullets: Applies to: medical laboratories developing their own management systems and demonstrating competence.
Also applicable to point-of-care testing (POCT), since the 2022 edition.
Used by accreditation bodies (like NABL) as the criteria for accrediting medical laboratories.

sections.heading: What the Standard Actually Requires
sections.body: ISO 15189 combines general quality-management requirements with technical/medical-specific competence requirements, covering the full patient-testing journey in student-friendly terms:
bullets: Personnel — documented competence, training, and authorisation for every role.
Facilities and environment — conditions suitable for the work performed (temperature, safety, space).
Equipment, reagents, and consumables — selection, calibration, maintenance, and acceptance criteria.
Pre-examination, examination, and post-examination processes — the same three phases covered in the NABL Medical Laboratories chapter.
Information management — how patient and quality data are handled, protected, and retained.
Risk management — identifying and controlling risks to patients and to result quality, aligned with dedicated risk-management standards for laboratories.
Nonconforming work, corrective action, and continual improvement — the same closed-loop cycle running throughout this subject.

sections.heading: Where This Sits in Cellfie
sections.body: Cellfie's ISO subject (Exam Prep → ISO) has a full standalone chapter walking through ISO 15189 clause-by-clause for anyone studying ISO generally. This chapter deliberately stays shorter and keeps its focus on why NABL uses this specific standard to accredit medical laboratories — the accreditation angle, not the full standard-mechanics angle.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: ISO 15189 is the international standard for medical laboratory quality and competence — the exact standard NABL assesses medical laboratories against. Current edition: ISO 15189:2022 (replaces the 2012 edition).
keyFacts: Current edition is ISO 15189:2022 — the 2012 edition is now historical/superseded.
The 2022 edition integrated point-of-care testing (POCT) requirements directly into the standard.
ISO 15189's 2022 structure was aligned with ISO/IEC 17025:2017's format.
ISO 15189 applies specifically to laboratories examining materials derived from the human body.
commonConfusion: ISO 15189 (medical laboratories) and ISO/IEC 17025 (testing/calibration laboratories) are structurally similar and both used by NABL — but they apply to different kinds of laboratories and are never interchangeable.

highYieldFacts: ISO 15189:2022 is the current edition; ISO 15189:2012 is historical.
NABL accredits MEDICAL laboratories specifically against ISO 15189, not ISO/IEC 17025.
POCT is now covered within ISO 15189 itself (since 2022), not a separate standard.
commonTraps: Citing ISO 15189:2012 as current in an exam — always check which edition a question implies.
Applying ISO 15189 to a general testing lab (chemical/environmental) instead of ISO/IEC 17025.
mustRemember: ISO 15189 → medical laboratories. ISO/IEC 17025 → testing and calibration laboratories.

confusedTerms.distinction: ISO 15189 covers medical laboratories examining human specimens for diagnosis/treatment. ISO/IEC 17025 covers general testing and calibration laboratories. Both are used by NABL, for different laboratory types.

comparisons.distinction: ISO 15189 is for medical laboratories (human specimen examination); ISO/IEC 17025 is for general testing and calibration laboratories. NABL uses both, for different accreditation programmes.

questions.prompt: Which standard is primarily associated with competence of medical laboratories?
questions.explanation: ISO 15189 is specifically the medical laboratories standard; the others cover reference materials, general testing/calibration, and proficiency testing respectively.

questions.prompt: What is the CURRENT edition of ISO 15189?
questions.explanation: ISO 15189:2022 is the current, fourth edition, replacing 2012.
